This appeal is preferred against the judgment and award dated 27.08.2003 passed by the learned Land Reference Court, Hingoli in L.A.R. No.93 of 1991.
2.

The appellants'/claimants' agricultural land situated at Village Pankanergaon, Tq. Sengaon, Dist.
Hingoli, bearing Block No. 246 admeasuring 2 H 69 Are, was acquired for the purpose of construction of a percolation tank of Village Pankanergaon, as per the notification issued and published under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, dated 29.12.1984.
The Land Acquisition Officer passed final award on 14.05.1988 and awarded compensation @ Rs. 33,865/- to the claimants for their acquired land.

The learned Reference Court enhanced the amount of 1 of 5 ((
2 )) 906 FA NO. 1437 OF 2003 compensation and awarded Rs. 6,000/- per acre.
Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the said compensation, the claimants have preferred the present appeal.
3. Learned advocate for the appellants pointed out the pleadings, the evidence, the grounds of objections in the appeal, and the reasons and findings in the impugned judgment.

He submitted that the learned Reference Court has not properly appreciated the evidence and while determining the compensation, the Reference Court applied guess work method which can be seen from paragraph No.7 of the impugned judgment.

He submitted that this Court in case of Dattatray Ananda Gugle and Others Vs. State of Maharashtra and another, passed in First Appeal No.1436 of 2003 and another connected appeal decided on 26.02.2026 relied upon the sale exemplar at Exhibit-35 by which the claimants therein were awarded compensation @ Rs.42,577/- per acre to their acquired Vithal Mahadji Zungare And Ors vs State Of Maha And Anr on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59723146/
1 lands which was acquired for the one and same purpose.

sentences.text: He pointed out the observations from the award of the Land Acquisition Officer, which show that there is existence of a well in land survey No.249/4.
He submitted that the said land is adjacent to the claimants' land from which the claimants were getting water facility for their land.

He 2 of 5 (( 3 )) 906 FA NO. 1437 OF 2003 further submitted that in view of the judgment of Chindha Fakira Patil (Dead) through LRs vs.
Special Land Acquisition Officer, (2006) 3 SCC 545, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that if there is irrigation facility available to the claimants' land, hence, it has to be treated as irrigated land, even if the claimants have not cultivated the crops like sugarcane, wheat, etc.

sentences.text: In such facts and circumstances, the claimants are entitled to compensation treating their land as irrigated land.
He therefore prayed to allow the appeal by enhancing the amount of compensation.
4. Learned AGP for the State strongly opposed the appeal and submitted that reasonable amount of compensation has been awarded to the claimants by the learned Reference Court.
The evidence was properly appreciated by the learned Reference Court which can be seen from paragraph Nos. 6 and 7 of the impugned judgment.

He further submitted that there is a long distance between Village Pankanergaon and village Nizampur, where the land under the sale exemplar at Exhibit-35 is situated, therefore, the said sale exemplar cannot be relied upon.
He prayed to dismiss the appeal.

5. Perused the Record and Proceedings, particularly the pleadings, the evidence, the grounds of objections of the appeal and 3 of 5 (( 4 )) 906 FA NO. 1437 OF 2003 the reasons and findings in the impugned judgment.

The observations of the valuer from the award of the Land Acquisition Officer shows that there was existence of a well in survey No.249/4, which is adjacent to the claimants'
land.
Crops such as sugarcane etc., were being cultivated there.
The evidence given in examination- in-chief before the Court was not shaken in the cross-examination.

On the basis of the valuer's observation regarding the existence of a well, and that the respondents have not disproved this evidence, it can be safely inferred that the adjoining land bearing Survey No. 249/4 had a well and that the claimants were using water facility from the same well.
In view of judgment in Chinda Fakira (supra), the claimants' land is certainly held as irrigated land.
The sale exemplar at Exhibit- 35 is squarely applicable to the present case and it is bonafide sale exemplar which was relied upon by this Court in First Appeal No.1436 of 2003 decided on 26.02.2026.

As per the said sale exemplar dated 26.03.1990, land admeasuring 2 H 10 Are was sold for a consideration of Rs.57,000/- i.e.,
Rs.633/- per Are.
Therefore, the claimants are certainly entitled to compesation @ Rs.633/- per Are.
The appeal therefore deserves to be allowed by setting aside the impugned judgment and award.

Hence, the following order:
4 of 5 (( 5 )) 906 FA NO. 1437 OF 2003 ::ORDER::
I.
The First Appeal is allowed.

II. The impugned judgment and award is set aside and  modified as under:
(a) The claimants are entitled to compensation @ Rs.633/-
per Are for their acquired land along with all statutory benefits like interest,
component and solatium etc., as per the Provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
